name: Jonathan
overview: Jonathan was a male figure known as the scribe in whose house the prophet Jeremiah was imprisoned, as recorded in Jeremiah 37:15. There is no tribal affiliation or additional personal details provided about him in Scripture. His role is noted specifically in connection with the prophet Jeremiah during a significant moment of prophetic ministry.
namesAndTitles: The name Jonathan means 'gift of YHWH,' reflecting a theophoric element common in Hebrew names. This proper name is mentioned in Jeremiah 37:15 and does not indicate that the name was given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for this Jonathan beyond his identification as the scribe who owned the house where Jeremiah was jailed. No other familial or relational details are provided.
scriptureSignificance: Jonathan's significance lies in his connection to the prophet Jeremiah, as the owner of the house where Jeremiah was confined. This association places Jonathan within the narrative of God's prophetic word during a turbulent period in Judah's history. While not a prominent character in his own right, his role as a scribe and host to Jeremiah underscores the practical support given to God's messengers.
